What "no seed oils" actually means

Seed and vegetable oils are some of the most common additives in processed food, and protein bars are no exception. This guide screens every bar for ten of them: canola, rapeseed, soybean, palm, palm kernel, palm fruit, sunflower, safflower, cottonseed, and corn oil, plus any bar listing generic "vegetable oil." High-oleic sunflower and safflower oil are permitted, since their fatty acid profile runs closer to olive oil than to the standard refined version of the same seed.

49% of the 1181 bars in our database fail this screen. Palm kernel oil is the single most common culprit, showing up 316 times, ahead of palm oil at 209. Both hide easily in a chocolate coating or a crispy layer, which is why a bar can look clean on the front of the package and still fail.

Palm kernel oil
Most common
Appears 316 times across the database, most often in a chocolate coating or as the base fat in a crisp layer.
Palm oil
Very common
Shows up 209 times, frequently as a coating fat or moisture retainer in mass-market bars.
Canola oil
74 bars
A cheap fat and moisture source. Tends to sit mid-list, easy to miss on a quick label scan.
High-oleic oils
Permitted
High-oleic sunflower and safflower oil have a different fatty acid profile and are not screened out here.

What we found screening 1181 bars

49%
of bars contain a seed or vegetable oil
581 of 1181 bars contain at least one of the ten oils we screen for. Palm kernel oil is the most common, ahead of palm oil and canola. It shows up in coatings, crisp layers, and as a base fat across brands at every price point.
Palm kernel oil hides in the coating, not the bar. Most bars that look clean at a glance use it in a chocolate shell or crisp layer rather than the base recipe, so it is easy to miss without reading the full ingredient list.
Wonderslim disqualifies almost entirely. 23 of 23 flavors fail, Vegetable oil and Palm kernel oil across the line.
Canola oil is the sneaky one. It shows up in bars that otherwise read clean, usually buried mid-list in a crispy layer or filling rather than called out up front.
Whole-food bars dominate the qualifying pool. RXBAR, Larabar, Thunderbird, Off the Farm, and Healthy Eating on the Go all qualify at 100%. Their fat comes from nuts, seeds, dates, or coconut rather than a refined oil.
A mixed lineup is common, not rare. 8 brands we checked split meaningfully between qualifying and disqualified flavors within the same lineup. KIND is the starkest case: 6 of 31 flavors qualify.
114 brands still represented. Even with 49% of the database disqualified, the qualifying pool covers a wide range of protein levels, price points, and grades.

Best brands for no seed oils

Seed oils turn up in brands you would not expect, and stay out of a few you might not guess either. These are the ones whose fat sources actually hold up, the ones that lean on them consistently, and the ones worth checking flavor by flavor.

Brands to target
  • Healthy Eating on the Go All 15 flavors qualify. Fat comes from peanut butter, nuts, and coconut, no processed oils anywhere in the line.
  • Larabar All 26 flavors qualify. Dates and nuts do the work, most flavors run four to six ingredients total.
  • Thunderbird All 14 flavors qualify, 9 of them A-grade. Fat comes from seeds, nuts, and coconut.
  • RXBAR All 12 flavors qualify. Egg whites, dates, and nuts, no oils of any kind added.
  • Transparent Labs All 7 flavors qualify with an average score of 10.2, among the highest of any brand on this list.
  • Elemental All 6 flavors qualify with an average score of 13.0, the top mark of any brand we track for this criterion.
  • Off the Farm All 5 flavors qualify. High protein without leaning on a refined oil for fat or texture.
  • B.T.R. Nation All 7 flavors qualify with an average score of 9.8. Consistent whole-food fat sources across the line.
  • Wild Zora All 5 flavors qualify. A meat-and-produce bar line that never reaches for a seed oil.
  • PEAK Protein All 3 flavors qualify, high protein and A-grade across the board.
  • Forward All 4 flavors qualify with an average score of 10.3. Smaller brand, clean across its whole lineup.
  • Send All 4 flavors qualify with an average score of 10.2. Smaller brand, clean across its whole lineup.
  • Kailo All 3 flavors qualify with an average score of 9.8. Smaller brand, clean across its whole lineup.
  • Tilt All 2 flavors qualify with an average score of 10.3. Smaller brand, clean across its whole lineup.
Brands to avoid
  • Wonderslim 23 of 23 flavors disqualified (100%). Vegetable oil and Palm kernel oil shows up across the line.
  • Barebells 23 of 25 flavors disqualified (92%). Sunflower oil and Soybean oil shows up across the line.
  • Pure Protein 18 of 18 flavors disqualified (100%). Canola oil and Palm oil shows up across the line.
  • FITCRUNCH 17 of 17 flavors disqualified (100%). Soybean oil and Sunflower oil shows up across the line.
  • One 15 of 15 flavors disqualified (100%). Palm kernel oil and Vegetable oil shows up across the line.
  • Fro Pro 15 of 15 flavors disqualified (100%). Palm fruit oil and Palm oil shows up across the line.
  • Lenny & Larry's 14 of 14 flavors disqualified (100%). Palm fruit oil and Palm oil shows up across the line.
  • Built 13 of 13 flavors disqualified (100%). Palm kernel oil and Palm oil shows up across the line.
  • Legendary 13 of 15 flavors disqualified (87%). Palm oil and Palm kernel oil shows up across the line.
  • Trubar 12 of 12 flavors disqualified (100%). Palm oil shows up across the line.
  • Power Crunch 11 of 11 flavors disqualified (100%). Palm kernel oil and Palm oil shows up across the line.
  • Clif Builders 10 of 10 flavors disqualified (100%). Palm kernel oil and Soybean oil shows up across the line.
Mixed lineups, check the flavor
  • KIND 6 of 31 flavors qualify, 25 do not. Fruit and Nut (B grade) is the clean pick, but check the label flavor by flavor.
  • NuGo 15 of 30 flavors qualify, 15 do not. Dark Chocolate Cherry (C grade) is the clean pick, but check the label flavor by flavor.
  • think! 3 of 22 flavors qualify, 19 do not. Peanut Butter Chocolate Chunk (B grade) is the clean pick, but check the label flavor by flavor.
  • Bobo's 15 of 21 flavors qualify, 6 do not. Peanut Butter Chocolate Chip Stuffd Oatmeal (C grade) is the clean pick, but check the label flavor by flavor.
  • Daryl's Bars 3 of 19 flavors qualify, 16 do not. Chocolate Mint (A grade) is the clean pick, but check the label flavor by flavor.
  • 1st Phorm 4 of 19 flavors qualify, 15 do not. Chocolate Brownie (A grade) is the clean pick, but check the label flavor by flavor.
  • Aloha 7 of 18 flavors qualify, 11 do not. Peanut Butter Chocolate Chip (B grade) is the clean pick, but check the label flavor by flavor.
  • GoMacro 13 of 17 flavors qualify, 4 do not. Dark Chocolate Almonds (B grade) is the clean pick, but check the label flavor by flavor.

Frequently asked questions

We screen for canola oil, rapeseed oil, soybean oil, palm oil, palm kernel oil, palm fruit oil, sunflower oil, safflower oil, cottonseed oil, corn oil, grapeseed oil, rice bran oil, and generic vegetable oil. High-oleic sunflower and safflower oil are permitted because their fatty acid profile is different from the standard refined versions.
No. All 12 RXBAR flavors qualify. RXBAR is built on egg whites, dates, and nuts, so the fat comes entirely from whole-food sources with nothing refined added.
No. All 26 Larabar flavors qualify. Most run four to six ingredients total, usually dates plus a nut or two, so there is no room for a seed oil to hide.
Some do. 6 of 31 KIND flavors qualify, including Fruit and Nut. The rest use palm kernel oil or canola oil, most often in a coating or crisp layer, so check the specific flavor rather than assuming the whole line is clean.
Bars with a chocolate coating or crispy layer are the most common offenders. Palm kernel oil is the single most frequent culprit across the database, ahead of palm oil and sunflower oil. It often shows up as "palm kernel oil" rather than plain "palm oil," so it is easy to miss on a quick label scan.
No. Coconut oil is not screened out by this guide. It comes from coconut flesh, not a seed, and has a different fatty acid makeup than the oils on our exclusion list. Bars using coconut oil or coconut butter qualify here.
High-oleic sunflower and safflower oils are permitted. They are bred for a high monounsaturated fat content, closer in profile to olive oil than to the standard refined version of the same seed. They are not treated as the same ingredient for this screen.
Yes, and it is more common than you would expect. NuGo splits almost exactly down the middle: 15 of 30 flavors qualify. Bobo's, GoMacro, and 1st Phorm all show the same pattern, usually because one flavor's coating or crisp layer uses a different fat source than the rest of the line. Always check the specific flavor, not just the brand.
We update the database whenever new bars are added or a brand reformulates. Manufacturers do change their ingredient lists over time, so always confirm against the packaging in front of you. This page reflects the database as of 2026-08-14.
Canola comes from rapeseed, which is a seed. We group it with the other refined seed and vegetable oils on this list for the same reason: a highly processed extraction method and a fatty acid profile heavier in omega-6 than whole-food fat sources like nuts, seeds, or dairy.
